proposal_for: PR-0008 AC-1 / AC-6 -- the route a REPAIRED bug takes to VERIFIED in this workshop, measured against the shipped automaton and approvals map at b7f282e
title: Der Schliessweg eines reparierten Bugs: pro Bug eine Nutzer-Muenzung, oder ein Weg, den die Werkstatt selbst gehen kann
context: MEASURED at b7f282e (kernel/backlog_types.AUTOMATA['BUG'], kernel/approvals.APPROVAL_TRANSITIONS, and `validate`'s own route line): OPEN -> TRIAGED (free) -> APPROVED (needs a user-minted 'scope' approval: one AskUserQuestion per bug, relayed verbatim by the lead) -> FIXED (free) -> VERIFIED (needs a passing 'test' Evidence that covers the bug; a declared selection run counts since DEC-0071). The terminals reachable WITHOUT a mint are REJECTED and DUPLICATE, and FR-0058 already names calling a repaired bug either of those a lie in the record. Generation 3 walked exactly four bugs this way (APR-0001..0004, BUG-0083..0086) and generation 4 one (APR-0006, BUG-0089). This stream's survey measures 188 active BUG items (89 pre-existing + 99 migrated holes; the order's '155' counts the archived holes too); the `validate` rollup at b7f282e already lists 28 of them as 'delivered but still open' (EVD-0036..0068 name them), and the survey adds every repaired one it re-measures. Every one of those needs ITS OWN scope mint before its Evidence can carry it to VERIFIED -- a click per bug for work the user already approved as part of the goals that shipped it (plan approvals APR-0005 / APR-0007). DEC-0051 (2) names 'den Freigabe-Weg in der Werkstatt nachruesten' as the goal and as its own round with its own security weighing -- not to be done on the side.

options.A: MINT PER BUG, as generation 3 did: the stream records the confirming Evidence (`evidence --kind test --result pass --related BUG-nnnn --run-command ... --run-scope selection`) and writes the re-measured chain into the item with `update`; the lead relays `request-approval scope BUG-nnnn` for every repaired bug in one sitting; after each mint `transition FIXED`, `transition VERIFIED`, `archive` are kernel lines anyone in the session can run. Cost: one question per bug (this survey: see the 'waits on the user' section of stream-protocol.md for the exact count), nothing in the kernel changes.
options.B: AN EDGE FOR THE CONFIRMED CASE: the BUG automaton gains TRIAGED -> FIXED as an extra edge (kernel/backlog_types), so a bug whose repair a passing test Evidence already proves walks to FIXED and then VERIFIED without a scope approval; the scope mint stays the route for a bug whose FIX is still to be built (APPROVED is what authorises fix work; DEC-0072's dispatch reads it). Cost: a spec-II.2 automaton change with its own DEC, a red-first test on the new edge, and the honest statement that the user then approves repaired bugs collectively through the goal that shipped them. Not built by this stream unless chosen -- it is the 'own round' DEC-0051 (2) reserves.
options.C: LEAVE THEM TRIAGED WITH THEIR EVIDENCE: the survey records the confirming Evidence and the chain, the items stay TRIAGED, and the AC-3 rollup ('stock lies upward') names every one of them with its route on every `validate`; the mint round is DEC-0051 (2)'s and happens when the user opens it. Cost: the status field keeps reading high while the derivation reads them closed -- the two-answers state FR-0058 measured, now with the derivation visible.

recommendation: A for this round (the shipped route, generation 3 proved it walks; the stream prepares every line so the user's part is the click), with B recorded as the question for DEC-0051 (2)'s own round. C only if the user does not want that many questions in one sitting -- then the AC-3 rollup is what keeps the debt visible.
what_the_user_decides: A (batch of mints, relayed by the lead), B (automaton edge, its own DEC), or C (Evidence recorded, status waits)
what_the_stream_does_meanwhile: records the Evidence and the re-measured chains for every repaired bug (needed under every option), archives what is already terminal, and lists the exact `request-approval scope BUG-nnnn` lines in stream-protocol.md
